   638:                                                               .kind = IR_TYPE_STRUCT,
   639:                                                               .field_count = 2,
   640:                                                               .is_complex = true,
   641:                                                           });
   642:     context->scalar_types[kind] = type;
   643:     return type;

   645: 
   646: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_scalar_type(CIrTypeContext* context, CTypeKind kind)
   647: {
   648:     if ((u32)kind >= C_TYPE_COUNT)
   649:     {
   650:         return IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
   651:     }
   652:     IrTypeId existing = context->scalar_types[kind];
   653:     if (existing.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
   654:     {
   655:         return existing;
   656:     }
   657:     if (c_type_kind_is_complex(kind))
   658:     {
   659:         return c_ir_complex_type(context, kind);
   660:     }
   661:     IrTypeKind ir_kind = IR_TYPE_COUNT;
   662:     u32 bit_width = 0;
   663:     bool is_signed = false;
   664:     u32 alignment = 0;
   665:     if (!c_ir_scalar_type_properties(context->target, kind, &ir_kind, &bit_width, &is_signed, &alignment))
   666:     {
   667:         return IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
   668:     }
   669:     // The IR layout of every scalar is the one c_parse_builtin_type_layout
   670:     // folds, `void` included: the two engines answer one question and this is
   671:     // the single table they both read. `void` is one byte aligned one there,
   672:     // which is what makes a `void *` step by bytes -- the pointer arithmetic
   673:     // below scales by the pointee's layout size and the incomplete-type
   674:     // refusal beside it tests that size for zero.
   675:     u64 size = 0;
   676:     u32 storage_alignment = 0;
   677:     if (!c_parse_builtin_type_layout(context->target, kind, &size, &storage_alignment))
   678:     {
   679:         return IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID;
   680:     }
   681:     alignment = storage_alignment;
   682:     IrTypeId type = ir_program_add_type(context->program, (IrType){
   683:                                                               .name = c_ir_scalar_type_name(kind),
   684:                                                               .element_type = IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID,
   685:                                                               .return_type = IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID,
   686:                                                               .layout =
   687:                                                                   {
   688:                                                                       .size = size,
   689:                                                                       .alignment = alignment,
   690:                                                                       .resolved = true,
   691:                                                                   },
   692:                                                               .kind = ir_kind,
   693:                                                               .bit_width = bit_width,
   694:                                                               .is_signed = is_signed,
   695:                                                               .is_nullptr = kind == C_TYPE_NULLPTR,
   696:                                                               .float_format = kind == C_TYPE_BFLOAT16 ? IR_FLOAT_FORMAT_BFLOAT16 : IR_FLOAT_FORMAT_IEEE,
   697:                                                           });
   698:     context->scalar_types[kind] = type;
   699:     if (ir_kind == IR_TYPE_INTEGER)
   700:     {
   701:         context->literal_limits[kind] = bit_width >= 64 ? (is_signed ? (u64)INT64_MAX : UINT64_MAX)
   702:                                         : is_signed     ? (((u64)1 << (bit_width - 1)) - 1)
   703:                                                         : (((u64)1 << bit_width) - 1);
   704:     }
   705:     return type;
   706: }
   707: 
   708: // Is this the type of an object C refuses to declare -- `void`, or an array of
   709: // it? The size above and completeness are different questions: GNU gives
